title: Bulk spectra and the non-Hermitian skin effect in systems with long-range couplings
authors: Jonathan Sturm, Pia Kreß, Adriana Pálffy
abstract: To achieve translational symmetry for the computation of the band structure of a lattice model, one can either consider an infinite lattice or impose periodic boundary conditions. While in sys- tems with short-range couplings these two approaches are equivalent, we show that for long-range couplings one can obtain considerably different results. We compare the two methods on the basis of one-dimensional quantum emitter chains both in free space and when coupled to a waveguide. The latter system allows for asymmetric couplings enabling the non-Hermitian skin effect, which we analyze using the two different band-structure calculation methods. We find that only periodic boundary conditions lead to physically and mathematically robust results, while the infinite-chain approach entails convergence issues and is unable to satisfyingly explain the emergence of the non- Hermitian skin effect in the waveguide system. In addition, the waveguide system yields unusual findings like a non-star shaped generalized Brillouin zone and strongly localized eigenstates with zero winding number.
summary: This paper rigorously compares two methods—infinite chain approximation versus periodic boundary conditions—for calculating band structures in quantum systems with long-range couplings. It demonstrates that for complex, non-Hermitian systems like emitters coupled to waveguides, the PBC approach is mathematically superior and necessary to correctly capture phenomena such as the non-Hermitian skin effect.
main_problem: The paper compares two distinct methods for calculating band structures in systems with long-range couplings, specifically addressing discrepancies that arise when translational symmetry is enforced.
main_result: For long-range couplings, the periodic boundary condition approach (Method II) yields physically and mathematically robust results, while the infinite chain approximation (Method I) fails to correctly describe phenomena like the non-Hermitian skin effect in waveguide systems.
method: The authors employ theoretical analysis comparing two summation methods: one assuming an infinite lattice ($\omega_I$) and another based on finite periodic boundary conditions ($\omega_{II}$).
model_or_system: The study uses one-dimensional quantum emitter chains, analyzed both in free space and when coupled to a waveguide. The Hamiltonian involves couplings $t_{ij}$ that can decay as short-range or long-range (power-law).
key_observables:
Band structure ($\omega(k)$), collective dipole shifts, decay rates ($\gamma(k)$), Generalized Brillouin Zone (GBZ), and the spectral winding number $
u(\epsilon_0)$.
important_parameters: The ratio of couplings controlling chirality ($\xi = \gamma_R/\gamma_L$) is crucial for inducing the non-Hermitian skin effect.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption tested is whether Method I and Method II converge, which they fail to do in the presence of long-range or chiral couplings in the waveguide setup.
figures_summary: Figures compare $\omega_I(k)$ vs. $\omega_{II}(k)$ for free space emitters (showing dipole shifts/decay rates) and illustrate the complex structure of the GBZ and limiting set ($\Lambda$) under strong chirality.
paper_structure: The paper develops by first establishing the general problem of long-range couplings, comparing Method I and II in simple models. It then applies this rigorous comparison to the more complex waveguide system, demonstrating where the methods diverge, culminating in an analysis of topological invariants like the winding number.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a critical methodological guide for theorists studying open quantum systems (like emitters coupled to waveguides) that exhibit non-Hermitian physics and long-range interactions. The distinction between infinite vs. periodic boundary conditions is a subtle but crucial theoretical point.
